narrationTexts: I'll find the remaining `db.query` call sites.
Pattern is clear. Applying it to the remaining files:
finalText:
Migration finished.

**Migrated — 12 files, 36 call sites** (`db.query(sql, params)` → `db.execute({ sql, params })`):

| Package | Files |
|---|---|
| accounts | `src/repo/session.js`, `src/service/teamService.js`, `src/admin/apiKeyAdmin.js` |
| billing | `src/repo/refund.js`, `src/service/couponService.js` |
| catalog | `src/repo/supplier.js`, `src/admin/variantAdmin.js` |
| orders | `src/repo/shipment.js`, `src/service/returnService.js` |
| support | `src/repo/sla.js`, `src/admin/macroAdmin.js` |
| analytics | `src/repo/cohort.js` |

All 12 pass `node --check`. The repo has no package.json or test suite, so syntax checking is the only verification available.

**Left alone, deliberately:**

- `vendor/legacy-orm/adapter.js` (2 call sites) — the file header says it's a vendored copy of legacy-orm 2.1.4, replaced wholesale on upgrade with local changes silently lost. Editing it would migrate the calls only until the next vendor bump. Since `lib/db.js` notes the driver's next major drops `query` entirely, this needs a real fix upstream or a wrapper at the boundary — flagging rather than patching.
- `cache.query(...)` (~25 call sites) — that's the cache handle in `lib/cache.js`, unrelated to the `db` object.
